intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SLC25A38 gene on chromosome 3p22.

checks.claim: Pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SLC25A38 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract links SLC25A38 mutations to recessive CSA. It does not say the mutations are homozygous or compound heterozygous, and it does not call the disorder pyridoxine-refractory.

checks.claim: The SLC25A38 gene is located on chromosome 3p22.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene the paper names.

paragraphs.text: Pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 is an autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia. It shows up early in life as severe microcytic, hypochromic anemia with ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow. Patients do not respond to pyridoxine, often need regular red cell transfusions and develop iron overload.

checks.claim: Pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 is an autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 presents early in life.
checks.evidence_quote: A female infant with congenital refractory sideroblastic anemia is described.
checks.explanation: The case is a congenital disorder in an infant, which supports early onset.

checks.claim: Pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 presents as severe microcytic, hypochromic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Their haemoglobin levels were 4.3 and 6.4 g/dl, respectively.
checks.explanation: The haemoglobin levels show the anaemia was severe. The abstract does not say the cells were microcytic or hypochromic.

checks.claim: Patients with pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 have ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow.
checks.evidence_quote: whose morphological hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts--bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria
checks.explanation: Ringed sideroblasts are described as the hallmark of sideroblastic anemias in general, not reported specifically for these patients.

checks.claim: Patients with pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 do not respond to pyridoxine.
checks.evidence_quote: which could explain the unresponsiveness to pyridoxine therapy in this case.
checks.explanation: The patient was refractory to pyridoxine.

checks.claim: Patients with pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 often need regular red cell transfusions.
checks.evidence_quote: had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth
checks.explanation: Both patients were transfusion dependent.

checks.claim: Patients with pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia-2 develop iron overload.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention iron overload.

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) studied patients with nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia from families showing autosomal recessive inheritance. These patients had severe microcytic, hypochromic anemia with ring sideroblasts in the marrow, and the anemia did not respond to pyridoxine.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) studied patients with nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia from families showing autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: by positional cloning, we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: Positional cloning of an autosomal recessive nonsyndromic CSA implies the authors studied families with recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The congenital sideroblastic anemia patients studied by Guernsey et al. (2009) had severe microcytic, hypochromic anemia.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no description of the patients' red cell indices or of how severe the anemia was.

checks.claim: The congenital sideroblastic anemia patients studied by Guernsey et al. (2009) had ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow.
checks.evidence_quote: whose morphological hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts--bone marrow erythroid precursors
checks.explanation: The abstract describes ringed sideroblasts as the hallmark of the disease class, not as a finding in these specific patients.

checks.claim: The anemia in the congenital sideroblastic anemia patients studied by Guernsey et al. (2009) did not respond to pyridoxine.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention a response to pyridoxine.

paragraphs.text: Kannengiesser et al. (2011) described more patients with SLC25A38-related congenital sideroblastic anemia. The anemia was severe and began early, most patients were transfusion dependent, and they developed iron overload that needed chelation therapy.

checks.claim: Kannengiesser et al. (2011) described additional patients with SLC25A38-related congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. This claim describes Kannengiesser et al. (2011), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: In the SLC25A38-related congenital sideroblastic anemia patients described by Kannengiesser et al. (2011), the anemia was severe.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. This claim describes Kannengiesser et al. (2011), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: In the SLC25A38-related congenital sideroblastic anemia patients described by Kannengiesser et al. (2011), the anemia began early.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. This claim describes Kannengiesser et al. (2011), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: Most SLC25A38-related congenital sideroblastic anemia patients described by Kannengiesser et al. (2011) were transfusion dependent.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. This claim describes Kannengiesser et al. (2011), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: The SLC25A38-related congenital sideroblastic anemia patients described by Kannengiesser et al. (2011) developed iron overload that needed chelation therapy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. This claim describes Kannengiesser et al. (2011), which this paper does not address.

paragraphs.text: The finding of homozygous or compound heterozygous SLC25A38 mutations in affected individuals (Guernsey et al., 2009) indicates that SIDBA2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

checks.claim: Homozygous or compound heterozygous SLC25A38 mutations were found in individuals affected with SIDBA2.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract reports mutations but does not specify homozygous or compound heterozygous zygosity.

checks.claim: SIDBA2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract states autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Congenital sideroblastic anemia is genetically heterogeneous. The X-linked pyridoxine-responsive form is caused by ALAS2 mutation, and SIDBA2 is an autosomal recessive form caused by SLC25A38 mutation.

checks.claim: Congenital sideroblastic anemia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: The sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematological disorders
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the group as heterogeneous, including acquired forms. Genetic heterogeneity of the congenital forms is only implied by 'previously unknown form'.

checks.claim: The X-linked pyridoxine-responsive form of congenital sideroblastic anemia is caused by ALAS2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: mutations of the erythroid-specific delta-aminolaevulinate synthase gene (ALAS2) at Xp11.21 have been reported in patients with X linked sideroblastic anaemia
checks.explanation: The abstract links ALAS2 mutations to X-linked sideroblastic anaemia but does not describe that form as pyridoxine-responsive.

checks.claim: SIDBA2 is an autosomal recessive form of congenital sideroblastic anemia caused by SLC25A38 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) used homozygosity mapping and candidate gene sequencing in families with autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia. They found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in SLC25A38, a gene for a mitochondrial carrier protein. Morpholino knockdown of the zebrafish ortholog caused anemia. Deleting the yeast ortholog (YDL119C) impaired synthesis of 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA). The authors proposed that SLC25A38 carries glycine into mitochondria for the first step of heme synthesis.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) used homozygosity mapping and candidate gene sequencing in families with autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, by positional cloning, we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions positional cloning only. It does not name homozygosity mapping or candidate gene sequencing.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) found homozygous or compound heterozygous SLC25A38 mutations in families with autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract reports SLC25A38 mutations but does not state their zygosity.

checks.claim: SLC25A38 encodes a mitochondrial carrier protein.
checks.evidence_quote: the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) found that morpholino knockdown of the zebrafish ortholog of SLC25A38 caused anemia.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention zebrafish morpholino experiments.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) found that deletion of the yeast SLC25A38 ortholog YDL119C impaired synthesis of 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention YDL119C or ALA synthesis. It says only that SLC25A38 is important for heme biosynthesis in eukaryotes.

checks.claim: Guernsey et al. (2009) proposed that SLC25A38 transports glycine into mitochondria for the first step of heme synthesis.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention glycine transport. It says only that SLC25A38 is important for heme biosynthesis.

paragraphs.text: Kannengiesser et al. (2011) found SLC25A38 mutations in further patients with congenital sideroblastic anemia. SLC25A38 was one of the most common genetic causes of the disorder after ALAS2.

checks.claim: Kannengiesser et al. (2011) found SLC25A38 mutations in additional patients with congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. This claim describes Kannengiesser et al. (2011), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: SLC25A38 was one of the most common genetic causes of congenital sideroblastic anemia after ALAS2.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not address how common the different genetic causes are, or ALAS2.

paragraphs.text: Patients do not respond to pyridoxine. Treatment relies on red cell transfusion and iron chelation. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation has cured some patients.

checks.claim: Patients with SIDBA2 do not respond to pyridoxine.
checks.evidence_quote: which could explain the unresponsiveness to pyridoxine therapy in this case.
checks.explanation: The patient did not respond to pyridoxine.

checks.claim: Treatment of SIDBA2 relies on red cell transfusion and iron chelation.
checks.evidence_quote: had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth
checks.explanation: Transfusion dependence is stated. The abstract does not mention iron chelation.

checks.claim: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation has cured some patients with SIDBA2.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention stem cell transplantation.
